 Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Dean Wade and Joel Embiid will start against the Raptors on Thursday.
 Wade will get the starting nod with LeBron James sidelined. This will likely be a singular start for Wade, though the 76ers do have a back-to-back coming up on Sunday and Monday, so Wade could be in line for another start.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Source:  Derek Bodner

 Joel Embiid (foot) is available to play against the Nets on Monday and will start alongside Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade. 
 Embiid will be back after sitting the first leg of Philadelphia’s back-to-back. Jabari Walker got the start in that one, so he will head back to the bench with Embiid back. Dean Wade will get the start next to Embiid in the frontcourt with LeBron James sitting the opposite leg of the back-to-back. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (back) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Nets. 
 As expected, James will sit out the second leg of a back-to-back set to manage his sciatica. In his absence, the Sixers could pivot to Kentavious Caldwell-Pope or Dean Wade to replace him in the starting five. 
 Jabari Walker 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #33 
 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said that Jabari Walker will start at center for the injured Joel Embiid (foot) on Sunday against the Pacers. 
 Due to injury management reasons, Embiid will not play on Sunday. Walker has been tabbed to fill the void, making him worth considering for streaming. Nurse also said that LeBron James and Dean Wade should also see time at the five in smaller lineups.

 Forward

 LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Pacers. 
 LeBron will be back for the first leg of the 76ers’ back-to-back. Dean Wade started in LeBron’s absence on Thursday, but with Joel Embiid (foot) ruled out on Sunday, Wade could remain the starter if they choose to start LeBron at center, which they did in one of Embiid’s two other absences this season.

 While Embiid appeared to tweak something in his left foot/ankle during Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics, his right foot has been an issue for longer. If he can’t play on Thursday, the 76ers could move Dean Wade into the starting lineup, while Jabari Walker would take on more responsibilities.

 Joel Embiid (foot) is probable for Sunday’s game against the Bulls. 
 Embiid is on the 76ers’ injury report for plantar fascia injury management, but the probable tag suggests he’ll be available. If he can’t play, the 76ers may start without a center, with Dean Wade moving into the starting lineup.

 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Bulls. 
 LeBron is back after missing Saturday’s win over the Hornets, the second game of a back-to-back. Who he pushes to the bench may depend on Joel Embiid (foot), who is questionable. If Embiid can play, Dean Wade would head to the bench. If Embiid can’t play, the 76ers could go without a true center, starting LeBron and Wade together, with Adem Bona on the bench.

 Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Dean Wade and Adem Bona will start Saturday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Brown is back after sitting out Friday’s win over the Knicks, but the 76ers are giving LeBron James and Joel Embiid the night off. As a result, Wade remains a starter, and Bona starts at center.

 Jaylen Brown (knee) is available for Saturday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Brown is good to go after sitting out Friday’s win over the Knicks. With LeBron James and Joel Embiid out, Dean Wade will likely start again after filling in for Brown on Friday.

 Paul George lit up the Magic with 22 points (7-of-13 FGs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and five three-pointers on Monday.
 George got off to a hot start to this game, scoring 10 of Boston’s 17 points in the first quarter. He cooled off after that, mostly because he didn’t see many shots. George only took four shots in the second half. Still, it was a solid game for him, though it could have been much more if he was used more. He’ll look to stay hot in Denver on Wednesday.

 Andrew Wiggins 
 MIA

 Andrew Wiggins recorded 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, three blocks and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Rockets.
 Wiggins’ slow start to the season led to his being removed from the starting lineup, a move that has benefited Miami’s first unit. With a sore hip sidelining Bam Adebayo at halftime, Wiggins returned to the starting lineup to begin the third quarter. He scored eight points in the second half, shooting 3-of-4 from the field, and added a steal and two blocks. Adebayo was sidelined for precautionary reasons, so he should be good to go for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. That would leave Wiggins on the bench; hopefully, he can be as productive as he was against the Rockets. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Player Stats

 Davion Mitchell dropped 16 points (7-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Rockets.
 After recording nine double-doubles in his first five NBA seasons, Mitchell is up to eight in 2026-27. “Off Night” shot 1-of-6 from three, but that was his only issue against the Rockets. Mitchell did not commit a turnover in his 33 minutes, and fantasy managers will be pleased with the four steals as well. Mitchell has exceeded expectations so far, and Miami’s lack of point-guard options behind him means his role is unlikely to change anytime soon. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Myron Gardner produced 14 points (5-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Rockets.
 With Pelle Larsson (illness) out, Gardner has started Miami’s last three games. After shooting 1-of-8 from three and scoring five points in the first two games, the undrafted wing matched his career high with 14 points, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. This was a good night for Gardner, but it shouldn’t sway the opinion of fantasy managers. Larsson said before Monday’s game that he expects to play Wednesday against the Bucks, so there’s little reason to add Gardner.
 -  Raphielle Johnson
